correctness.rationale: The visible facet projections partition the shadow up to area-zero boundaries, so projected area is the sum of positive outward area-vector dot products, equivalently half their absolute sum by vector balance. The base area vector is (0,0,-4ab); side pairs are (±bh,0,ab) and (0,±ah,ab). Pairing absolute values and expanding the two maxima yields exactly the 18 support forms. The largest vector norm is attained only at its own oriented unit direction. Squared candidate norms cross at s²=7, 5r² and 12r²/(1+r²); their order changes at r²=7/5. The other one-sided family is strictly shorter when r>1, and when r=1 both one-sided families lie below the envelope because the diagonal family exceeds the axial one before s²=7. Thus the phase counts, including fourteen at the triple point, are exhaustive. Above the certified q no nonwinning vector contributes; two winning caps cannot meet in their interiors because their simultaneous inner products would exceed half the norm of the sum. Each cap has normalized area (1-t/M)/2. There are no atoms (a level set lies in a finite union of planar sections of the sphere), so independence gives the maximum limit as stated.
residual_risks: The cap threshold q is sufficient, not asserted optimal; the proof is analytic, not a formal certification.
